evidence: PUBLIC INSTRUCTION - achievable and single-reading on every graded point checked. Reachability: everything the brief asks for is buildable offline from the pinned agent image (environment/Dockerfile: node:22-bookworm-slim, express@5.1.0 + better-sqlite3@12.4.1 under NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules) and the seed; no capability needs the internet. test.sh:104-111 launches with exactly PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT=3000, DB_PATH, matching hireops_rules.md section 8 and instruction.md:13. Seed supports every seeded fact the criteria quote: 10 users with the roles listed in instruction.md:17; Platform Engineer Applied Greta/Ade/Marco (positions 1-3) and Screen Priya/Samuel; APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'; APP-101 has 120 messages (app_context.md:30) with unique monotone created_at; Lena APP-301 has 3 messages with read_count 2 and message 3 from USR-REC3, so unread=1 as protocol Z states; candidate_status_labels and thread_page_size=30 are in the seed as hireops_rules.md:208-209 says. Rule-level unambiguity: the stale-move ABA test (protocol C, F moved back to Applied by Mei then the old Applied->Screen request replayed) is decided by an explicit rule, 'Every card carries a version that changes whenever the card moves' (hireops_rules.md:77), so an expected-from-stage-only design is not a second reasonable reading. Bulk arrival order (rules:89-92), undo place/once/conflict/overfill (rules:94-100, notes do not count), hiring-manager late-stage set incl. re-order and reject/reopen limits (rules:70-72), 401/403/404 statuses (rules:21-23), unread definition and scrolled-up behaviour (rules:151-160), seen definition incl. Observer exclusion (rules:164-166), drafts per person/conversation/browser surviving session end and other sign-ins (rules:170-175; notes 'kept ... until it is saved' rules:106), candidate wording and data exclusions (rules:183-194), places 1..50 whole numbers (rules:28) all map one-to-one onto criteria hro_* with no extra hidden demand found. I walked protocols M, L and B(1)-(15) step by step: every expected outcome (e.g. B(5) Applied Y,W,X,Z,A2; B(12) Mei moving Y down one place in Screen W..A2 leaves A2's index 4 untouched so the undo legitimately goes ahead; B(13) arrival A2,V; L undo refused only by overfill) follows from the rules under the single reading. Underspecified-but-harmless points (both readings pass the criteria): whether re-ordering/rejection are themselves undoable 'moves' (no protocol step distinguishes), whether a hiring manager can view other jobs' boards/notes (hro_mgr_other_job and hro_notes accept 'not offered' or 'refused'), unread for never-opened conversations (graded only as deltas or after sending, which counts as read), what 'looks like an email' means (judge chooses the invalid value), and instruction.md:9 'or anyone else' vs rules:192 'other candidates' (rules narrow it; staff names in a candidate's own conversation are fine). Workbook-sheet conflict noted: Internal sheet says 'no network', public sheet and skill profile say network allowed; the task needs none, so no impact. RISK (environment-level, outside the brief's text but within 'try a conforming alternative that could fail'): hireops_rules.md:158 says a message arriving while a person is at the newest message 'is shown and counts as read', and rules:165 makes a staff message seen once the candidate 'has had the conversation open at or after that message'. Functional protocol U (prompt.md:41) has Tomas send messages from his independent context (so his conversation is open at its newest) and then: 'Rafael then sends a new message: it shows as not seen; Aud opens the conversation: still not seen; Tomas opens it: seen' - without telling the judge to close Tomas's context or navigate it away first. The golden itself does exactly what the rule says: public/js/app.js:142 opens an EventSource and threads.js:157 'if (stay) { toBottom(); paint(c); if (theirs && active) markRead(id); }', so Tomas's still-open page marks Rafael's message read within about a second and Rafael's page shows 'Seen' before Aud opens -> hro_seen (weight 1.5) 'Fails if seen is shown too early ... after only the Observer'. The same pattern recurs later in U: Bill opens the conversation, and if his context stays open Tomas's next message is seen by Bill before 'Rafael opens it'. Whether this bites depends on whether the judge closes each independent context after use (the boilerplate 'close only ctx afterwards' suggests so but is not tied to U's steps). The raw evidence (workspace.cjs lines 263-273, 425) drives seen via direct API calls and a single receipt wait, not U's judge ordering, so the hazard is NOT EXERCISED. No configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index scope says so); none is claimed here.
counterexample: Rule-conforming app (and the golden, per threads.js:157 + app.js:142): judge follows U literally, keeps Tomas's independent page open on the J2 conversation after 'Tomas sends one more', then Rafael sends. Tomas's open-at-newest page receives it over SSE and marks it read (as hireops_rules.md:158/165 require), so Rafael's receipt reads 'Seen' before Aud opens; the judge records 'seen shown after only the Observer' and gives hro_seen 0 to a correct app. A weak app that only marks read on an explicit open click would pass the same step - the protocol rewards the less conforming behaviour.
suggested_fix: In functional prompt.md protocol U, explicitly close (or navigate away from the conversation in) Tomas's independent context before Rafael sends, and close Bill's context after he opens the conversation, before Tomas's next message; then confirm with a configured judge run on the golden. No change to the public instruction is needed.
